title: Returned-Payment Fees and the Home-Site Lease Renewal Increase
content:
Under Home-Site Lease renewal pricing, a returned-payment adjustment, in percentage points, is added to the renewal increase rate of the renewal offer. It counts the returned-payment fees posted on the lease with an entry date in the trailing 12 calendar months, read on the day the offer is issued.

**Rule applied by the desk.** With two or more such returned-payment fees the adjustment is 1.0 percentage point; with exactly one it is 0.5 percentage points; with none it is zero. A positive adjustment raises the renewal increase rate by that many points.

| Returned-payment fees posted in the trailing 12 calendar months | Returned-payment adjustment |
|---|---|
| two or more | 1.0 percentage point higher |
| exactly one | 0.5 percentage points higher |
| none | zero |

**Points of judgement**

- *What is counted?* Returned-payment fees posted on the lease's rent ledger, by their entry date. A fee posted before the trailing 12 calendar months is outside the count.
- *Where do the rows divide?* Between none and one (zero against 0.5) and between one and two (0.5 against 1.0). Three or more fees give the same 1.0 as two.

**Hypothetical applications** (renewal increase rate of 5.0 percent assumed for illustration)

| Returned-payment fees in the window | Adjustment | Rate after this adjustment |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | 5.0 percent |
| 1 | 0.5 | 5.5 percent |
| 3 | 1.0 | 6.0 percent |
